newsitem.title: INDIA: India soymeal prices rise on firm overseas demand.
newsitem.headline: India soymeal prices rise on firm overseas demand.

text.p: Good overseas demand and poor soybean arrivals have pushed up Indian soymeal export prices by nearly $10 in the last four days, traders said on Friday.
"There is good gemand for Indian soymeal and prices may further increase due to limited availability," said S.N. Saboo, a leading oilmeal broker.
Traders said Indian soymeal exporters had contracted to export around 650,000 tonnes of soymeal during November, December and January.
They said soymeal was currently quoted at $262-264 per tonne fob, up from around $255 on Monday.
Soybean arrivals had dropped to nearly 1,500 tonnes per day from 4,000 tonnes last week in the markets of central India, the hub of India's soybean industry.
Continous rains during the last few days had disrupted the soybean harvest in the central state of Madhya Pradesh, traders said.
Soybean prices, in the local markets, had risen to around 9,850-10,100 rupees per tonne from around 9,500-9,750 rupees in the last three days, they said.
